replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: I respect that you have a different interpretation. For this video I’m sticking to the geological evidence for Folded Mountain, sedimentary layers compressed, folded and uplifted during the formation of the Rockies. One small correction, though: carbon-14 isn’t used to determine the age of rocks this old. It’s mainly used for once-living material up to about 50,000 years; geologists use other radiometric methods for much older rocks.

comments.author: @ErksumSpiffly
comments.text:
I have seen folded rocks in a few formations in the Rockies but this is next level. They help me to connect my ideas with geological time.
Can you find interesting facts about the existence of a temperate rainforest at Mount Robson? Also, giant TNT blasts near Suffield, Alberta throughout the 1960s. My grandfather wrangled test animals for some of the events.

replies.author: @ErksumSpiffly
@HiddenCanada
replies.text: Those are two fantastic rabbit holes. The Robson Valley has one of the world’s rare inland temperate rainforest ecosystems, and Suffield is even wilder, Canada actually detonated 500-ton TNT charges there during major blast experiments in the 1960s. Your grandfather wrangling test animals for some of those events is an incredible connection. If you know which tests or roughly what years he worked there, I’d love to hear more.

comments.author: @greenmanofkent
comments.text: Why have a thumbnail headlined "Rocks don't bend" when the video shows very clearly (and correctly) that they do!?

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: “Rocks Don’t Bend” was meant to represent the obvious first reaction before the video explains how they actually can bend, slide and fault over millions of years.
